title: Challenges Of Integrating Responsible Management Education In Higher Education Institutions Of Uttar Pradesh, India
abstract: India is facing a big debate on various social, economic and political issues which remained around corruption and poverty; how they can be eradicated from our society. Uttar Pradesh (U.P.) is the most populous state of our country with over 16.4 % of countries total population. Moreover with 9% of the country’s total geographical area, U.P. is the 4th largest state of our country. The median age of U.P. is 20 whereas that of India is young 24 years as in 2011. Though U.P. is the youngest state in India and has a rich cultural heritage but when it comes to literacy and gross enrolment in higher education, it is far behind other states. In order to create a responsible environment, management education can work as a very effective tool. In order to tackle the challenges faced globally such as corruption, poverty and workforce diversity, the United Nations has developed Responsible management initiative. The objective of this paper is to present the structure and different channels of management education in India with special reference to U.P. state. The focus is on identifying critical factors in integrating responsible management education in Higher Educational institutions with reference to sustainable development.

title: Women Empowerment and Livelihood Opportunities through Homebased Handicraft Activities
abstract: So as to improve their social and health position and encompass them in progressive accomplishments. Empowerment as delegation of supremacy to somebody has been a way to enrich individual and work life value of woman in current decades. Higher education and livelihood are effective mechanism to women empowerment, but culture roles and inspiration can’t be denied. Cultural heritage personified in traditional artistries is an essential measure of any state that reveals the culture and radiation of the region. The handicrafts sector shows a vigorous character on income and generations of employment and has also been familiar globally due to poverty lessening. In KP’s culture, it is habitual to clarify some craftworks to girls. It is common in educated and illiterate families, but illiterate families focus more on it. The joint crafts skilled to girls are embroidery, Mezari, sewing, quilts, applique, crochet, knitting etc. This paper recognizes how to empower women of Village Aka Khel (Upper Kurram) from poverty over creative industry of handicrafts. Numerous recommendations are established for how creative industry can contribute in empowerment of women. The limitation of this research is to conduct at innovative industry. title: Singing Bowl an unsung handicraft of Bankura, West Bengal, India
abstract: Bankura district has long cultural heritage in making of beautiful and world-famous handicrafts. Terracotta, Dokra, Stone Curving, Wood Curving, Weaving is few examples among them. But besides these well-known handicrafts, ‘Singing Bowl’ remains unsung to everybody. It is an outstanding handicraft making of alloy at various places of this district and the state of West Bengal. This bowl can have made from bell and brass metal. In the past, these bowls were use in worships of God, for holistic rituals, and domestic use. But presently this bowl is using in medical sound therapy and music. For the sound therapy and sound healing this bowl become an international interest of trade. The study shows that, in Pukhuria moza of Simlapal block, Bankura District currently around 250 households engaged in making of Singing Bowl. The artisans have to work hard throughout the year to meet the ever-increasing global needs but their economic condition remains unsatisfactory. Therefore, in this work we are trying to understand the making and marketing process of the singing bowl, economic dichotomies between artisans and traders and also to find a sustainable way to attain the sustainable livelihood for all.

title: ANALYSING THE CAUSES AND MITIGATION STRATEGIES OF TRAGIC TALE; THE HUMAN – TIGER CONFLICTS IN GARHWAL HIMALAYAN REGION OF UTTARAKHAND
abstract: Garhwal Himalayan region is a biodiversity hotspot with a rich wildlife and cultural heritage, including tigers, leopards and other wild animals. However, the increasing number of human-tiger conflicts in this region pose a significant threat to both human livelihoods and tiger conservation. This study assesses the causes of human-tiger conflicts in Garhwal Himalayan region and evaluates the effectiveness of existing mitigation strategies with a new look to better preventive measures. The underlying causes of these conflicts, emphasizing anthropogenic pressures and eventual interventions, habitat fragmentation and socio-economic factors have further been explored with greater degree of intensity. Through a comprehensive review of existing literature and case studies, this research communication endeavours to offer better explanation for this tragic/pathetic situation including devising better and effective strategies for mitigating this crisis. The existing gaps in current mitigation measures have also been underlined with a proposal of multi-stakeholder approach to address the issue. Our findings and recommendations will enable the policy makers and people involved in the conservation processes to reduce this painful two- edged sharp sword of human-tiger conflicts and promote the coexistence concept of togetherness for sustained survival.

title: Forecasting Regional Tourist Influx with Decision Tree Regression and GRNN: A Data-Driven Approach
abstract: Kumaun, a renowned region in Uttarakhand, attracts a large number of tourists annually due to its natural beauty and rich cultural heritage. The influx of tourists varies significantly with the seasons, with certain months experiencing higher footfall than others. This study aims to predict tourist arrivals in the region using various factors such as month, temperature, number of local events, and hotel prices. A preexisting dataset comprising 100 records was utilized for the analysis. Two predictive models were developed: Decision Tree Regression and Generalized Regression Neural Network (GRNN). The performance of both models was evaluated using standard metrics including Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and the Coefficient of Determination (R2). The Decision Tree Regression model demonstrated moderate predictive capability with an R2score of approximately 44.94%, whereas the GRNN model underperformed, yielding a negative R2value. Based on these results, the Decision Tree model is considered more suitable for this application. The findings of this study may assist government bodies and tourism authorities in better planning and resource management during peak and off-peak tourist seasons.

title: Role of Religious Tourism in Balanced Economic Growth
abstract: In India, religious tourism plays a vital role in narrowing economic imbalance. Most of the places, especially rural areas and the areas which have no core competence or business, survive due to religious tourism. It provides business and employment opportunities to local population helps to take care of their requirements.Religious tourism, one of the oldest forms of human mobility, has emerged as a significant component of the global tourism industry. It integrates cultural heritage, spiritual enrichment, and economic development. Religious tourism — travel motivated by pilgrimage, faith, and spiritual experience — is a rapidly growing and economically significant sub-sector of global tourism. This paper examines how religious tourism contributes to balanced economic growth through job creation, MSME stimulation, infrastructure development, regional redistribution of income, and cultural entrepreneurship while also identifying risks (overcrowding, seasonal volatility, environmental stress). Using a mixed-methods framework (secondary data analysis from national tourism accounts, sector reports, and case studies) the study synthesizes empirical findings and proposes policy instruments that maximize inclusive, sustainable benefits of religious tourism for local and national economies.

title: SACRED LOTUS: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF ITS FUNCTIONAL USES
abstract: The sacred lotus (Nelumbo nucifera Gaertn.), India's national flower, symbolizes purity, beauty, wisdom and immortality. The lotus, a perennial rhizomatous aquatic plant renowned for its large floating leaves and vibrant flowers, is distributed globally and cultivated for over 3,000 years. It holds a prominent position in history and cultural traditions, particularly in Hinduism and Buddhism. The sacred lotus is more than just a symbol, it offers wide range of ecological, economic, and nutraceutical benefits. Almost all parts of the lotus have both edible and medicinal uses, highlighting its deep cultural and religious significance. Beyond its nutritional and medicinal benefits, the lotus plant's stem produces fine fibers known as "Lotus Silk," which creates eco-friendly fabrics with antibacterial, self-cleaning, and superhydrophobic qualities. These characteristics collectively emphasize the lotus's diverse contributions to horticulture and its sustainable use contributes significantly to human welfare through its harmonious relationship with nature. This review explores the functional uses of lotus plant, emphasizing its role in promoting environmental sustainability, cultural heritage, horticultural significance and innovative applications in various industries

title: The Role of Theatre Artists in the Development, Preservation, and Promotion of Telugu Theatre in Kadapa District: A Study
abstract: Theatre is one of the oldest performing arts that reflects the cultural, social, and historical identity of a society. Kadapa District (YSR District), Andhra Pradesh, has played a significant role in the development of Telugu theatre through the dedication of numerous theatre artists, drama organizations, and traditional performing groups. The district is widely recognized as the birthplace of the Surabhi Theatre movement, which has preserved mythological, historical, and social dramas for more than a century. Theatre artists from Kadapa have contributed immensely as actors, directors, playwrights, musicians, stage designers, costume designers, and cultural educators. Their efforts have promoted Telugu language, literature, and cultural heritage while inspiring future generations. However, modernization, digital entertainment, and financial challenges have adversely affected traditional theatre. This study examines the contributions of theatre artists toward the development, preservation, and promotion of Telugu theatre in Kadapa District. Using historical and descriptive research methods, the study analyzes their artistic achievements, cultural significance, institutional support, and contemporary challenges. The findings emphasize the need for documentation, digital preservation, financial assistance, and policy support to ensure the sustainability of Telugu theatre

title: Enterprenuerial Challenges Of Rural Women Of Pochampally Mandal - A Case Of Social Innovaton
abstract: Rural women’s entrepreneurial activities play a critical role in economic development and in preserving traditional crafts. The women weavers of Pochampally, Telangana—renowned for their Ikat sarees—are skilled artisan-entrepreneurs, yet many struggle to achieve economic independence and sustainable growth because of substantial marketing barriers. Key challenges include limited digital literacy, weak branding, restricted market access, and stiff competition from massproduced and mechanized imitations. Additional constraints are slow technology adoption and sparse use of e-commerce platforms. To capture the lived experiences of these women, this study uses a mixed-methods approach—combining surveys with focus groups and in-depth interviews—and relies on qualitative case analysis. Findings indicate that despite exceptional craftsmanship and a rich cultural heritage, Pochampally’s women weavers require targeted interventions: training in digital and marketing skills, support for brand development, improved access to online and offline markets, and government and NGO initiatives to protect intellectual property and counter mechanized knockoffs. The study concludes that coordinated action by stakeholders is essential to sustain Pochampally Ikat in competitive global markets and to empower rural women entrepreneurs through socially innovative solutions.

title: Traditional Culture of Koli Fishing Community in Thane (Konkan Region)
abstract: Abstract The Konkan coastal region of Maharashtra has historically been inhabited by the Koli fishing community, one of the earliest indigenous coastal communities in western India. The traditional lifestyle, occupation, and cultural practices of the Kolis are closely connected with the sea, forming an important part of the region’s cultural heritage. This paper focuses on the traditional culture of the Koli fishing community in Thane district, which forms a significant part of the Konkan coastal belt.The study examines various aspects of Koli cultural life, including traditional fishing practices, community rituals, festivals, and social customs that have shaped their identity over generations. It also highlights the important role played by community members, especially women, in sustaining both economic and cultural activities. In recent decades, however, rapid urbanization, coastal development, and changing occupational patterns have influenced traditional lifestyles and cultural continuity.The paper emphasizes the importance of documenting and preserving the traditional cultural practices of the Koli community in order to protect the cultural diversity of the Konkan region. Understanding these traditions is essential for ensuring that development and modernization do not lead to the gradual disappearance of indigenous coastal heritage.

title: From Capture to Engagement: A Reproducible Workflow for 360° Virtual Tours and Audience Evaluation of Sacred Kerala Temple Murals
abstract: Abstract Documenting reproducible workflows is a recognized gap in Digital Humanities scholarship, particularly for sacred heritage digitization where tacit methodological decisions around ethics, capture, authoring, and evaluation are rarely made explicit. This paper addresses that gap through a fully documented, pipeline for creating and assessing 360° virtual tours of Kerala temple murals, demonstrated through the Chemmanthatta Mahadeva Temple, Thrissur, central Kerala. What distinguishes this workflow from comparable digital heritage projects is the intersection of three methodological commitments rarely combined in a single pipeline: (1) ethically governed capture of a living, ritually active sacred site; (2) darśan-sensitive authoring that preserves the spatial and devotional logic of the temple interior; and (3) an embedded audience evaluation instrument designed to measure culturally specific perceptions of aura, sacredness, and authenticity in a virtual environment. Together, these commitments surface the “hidden costs” of sacred heritage digitization that standard workflows leave unaddressed. The workflow comprises five documented stages. In the first stage, Ethical Capture, permission had to be obtained from both local temple administration and Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), Thrissur Circle. ASI regulations mandated certain requirements regarding the placement of cameras, use of flash photography, and entry into the sanctum sanctorum itself, all of which were respected and included in the workflow process; specifically, the ritual lines of sight involving the deepasthambham and balipeetham were retained in the panoramic views. Community approval protocols were used to allow for publishing of devotional images and minimize participant responses. In the second stage, Contextual Authoring, panoramas of 360° views were edited in Affinity Photo 2 and imported into Articulate Storyline 360, chosen because of its hotspot navigation tools and minimal coding required for humanities scholars. The final product will offer annotations about mural iconography but maintain the temple experience from entry to sanctum. If a team does not have access to Articulate Storyline 360, the pipeline was designed with enough detail to recreate using open-source software options such as Pannellum or A-Frame. Thirdly, evaluation design incorporates the implementation of a purpose-designed survey embedded directly into the tour. The measurement tool includes ten items measuring on a Likert scale three constructs: aura/presence, sacredness/reverence, and authenticity/fidelity, along with two additional items for comparing physical and virtual darśan. Aura is defined and operationalized based on the ritualized embeddedness approach suggested by Benjamin, elaborated by Kenderdine and Yip in terms of digital facsimile; sacredness is based on the definition of darśan as a relational experience with a divine image by Eck; and authenticity is understood and measured from both material (accuracy of reproduction) and experiential (genuineness of experience) perspectives. The definitions have been developed specifically to consider cross-cultural differences in perceptions, as some respondents are likely to perceive the above-mentioned constructs from the perspective of people unfamiliar with Kerala temple culture. The fourth stage was the deployment and data collection process where the tour had been hosted on the web. Data have been collected using n=100 individuals who came from a diverse community made up of professionals in heritage, art history students, and general public. The backgrounds of the participants were captured as covariates to test the effect that previous knowledge of darśan has on perceived virtual sacredness. This could minimize novelty bias by acclimating the participant to the 360° interface before evaluation questions were asked. Analysis and Archiving: The fifth phase involved exporting descriptive statistics in CSV format and coding the qualitative answers manually. Analysis so far reveals that respondents with experience with temple worship felt higher levels of sacredness and presence but authenticity was relatively consistent, implying that visual realism is more universal compared to the experience of worshiping. All assets used in this project are version-controlled at GitHub under the CC BY-SA 4.0 license, including panoramas, 360 Storyline template with its branching, survey form as an independent Google Form, raw data schema. Portability is an essential consideration in the workflow design. The five-step process can be generalized from this particular temple; any team engaging with a heritage site that requires institutional clearance, spatial reasoning, and culturally sensitive appraisal can leverage this model. Chemmanthatta temple is only a concrete example of the more generalizable process rather than a special case. Through articulation of the ASI negotiating protocols, darśan-oriented UX design principles, and consent-based approaches inherent in similar projects but usually unspoken of, we aim at developing an ethically sustainable virtual heritage system consistent with DARIAH's approach.

title: The Role of Geographical Indication Tags in Enhancing Regional Development in India
abstract: Geographical Indication Tags have emerged as a pivotal tool for promoting regional development in India by protecting and promoting products linked to a specific geographical origin. This enhance economic status, preserve cultural heritage, and foster sustainable development within local communities. The conferment of GI tags increase the market value and recognition of region specific goods, leading to job creation, greater income for producers by premium pricing and access to new markets, and promotion of traditional knowledge and skills. It also prevents rural exodus by stimulating local economies, encourages cultural tourism by creating distinctive regional brands, and support environmental stewardship through conservation of traditional and sustainable production practices. Despite these benefits, there are various challenges faced in the registration, protection and enforcement of GI tags which may limit the effective realization of GI potential in India. This research article evaluates the opportunities, barriers, possible solutions to overcome these barriers and schemes/initiatives for promoting GI tags in India. All these offers insights for policymakers and stakeholders to harness GI tags as a catalyst for inclusive and sustainable growth, cultural preservation and long term socio-economic advancement in Indian regions.

title: Reclaiming the Silenced Past: A Postcolonial Reading of Sally Morgan’s My Place
abstract: Australia today is acknowledged as a multicultural and multiethnic democracy. However, its history of a quarter millennium ago is neither spotless nor unblemished. Numerous heterogeneous Aboriginals tribes inhabited this island region for about 40,000 years until 1788. Nonetheless, their proportion of the total population in Australia has decreased to approximately 3.8% now. The missing 96.2% of Aboriginal population needs to be accounted for. The predominant narrative, woven by white scholars with a predominant Eurocentric viewpoint, conveniently ignores such uncomfortable enquiries. It distorts Australian history and culture, glorifying the colonisers who hoisted the Union Jack on the native land in 1788. The indigenous Aboriginal tribes were portrayed as savage heathens in urgent need of reform, civilisation, culture, and religion. It was used as an alibi to displace, dispossess, subjugate and annihilate the numerous native tribes. A small number of Indigenous populations, who have successfully achieved upward social mobility assume the crucial role of advocating for their community by sharing their narrative, historical experiences, cultural heritage, the injustices they have endured and continue to face and how they envision a dignified future. In this context, the present paper is a reading of one such life-writing by an Aboriginal woman, My Place by Sally Morgan.

title: Ethnomedicinal and Phytochemical Studies on Sacred Plants of Eastern and Northern India
abstract: Sacred groves in India represent a unique convergence of cultural heritage, ecological sustainability, and traditional healthcare practices. These community-managed forest patches safeguard plant species that hold both religious and therapeutic significance. However, these are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic pressures. The study highlights the ethnomedicinal values of these sacred groves through documentation, phytochemical profiling, and quantitative estimation of total phenols and flavonoids. Sacred groves from Odisha, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Bihar were surveyed between 2023-2024, documenting 12 sacred medicinal plants from 11 different families. Qualitative phytochemical analysis revealed the presence of various bioactive secondary metabolites, including alkaloids, flavonoids, phenols, saponins, tannins, and terpenoids. Quantitative assays showed that Emblica officinalis exhibited the highest total phenolic content at 4.86 mg/100 g, while Ocimum sanctum had the highest flavonoid concentration at 2.18 mg/100 g. These findings emphasise the dual ecological and pharmacological importance of sacred plants, underscoring the need for sustainable conservation efforts and the integration of traditional knowledge with modern healthcare systems.

title: Traditional Culture of Koli Fishing Community in Thane (Konkan Region)
abstract: Abstract The Konkan coastal region of Maharashtra has historically been inhabited by the Koli fishing community, one of the earliest indigenous coastal communities in western India. The traditional lifestyle, occupation, and cultural practices of the Kolis are closely connected with the sea, forming an important part of the region’s cultural heritage. This paper focuses on the traditional culture of the Koli fishing community in Thane district, which forms a significant part of the Konkan coastal belt.The study examines various aspects of Koli cultural life, including traditional fishing practices, community rituals, festivals, and social customs that have shaped their identity over generations. It also highlights the important role played by community members, especially women, in sustaining both economic and cultural activities. In recent decades, however, rapid urbanization, coastal development, and changing occupational patterns have influenced traditional lifestyles and cultural continuity.The paper emphasizes the importance of documenting and preserving the traditional cultural practices of the Koli community in order to protect the cultural diversity of the Konkan region. Understanding these traditions is essential for ensuring that development and modernization do not lead to the gradual disappearance of indigenous coastal heritage.

title: Traditional foods consumed by tribal communities of India
abstract: Geographical, cultural, and environmental factors have all had a role in shaping the culinary traditions of India's many distinct tribal communities, each of which has its own distinctive culinary traditions. The culture and social practices of indigenous tribes around the world are inextricably linked to the traditional foods found in those areas. The production of many of these foods involves the use of organic, nutrient-dense, and ecologically sustainable ingredients derived from the immediate vicinity. Tribal cuisine, which spans from rice-based meals to millet-based recipes, reflects traditional food systems that emphasise balance, seasonal foods, and natural food preservation. A vast range of local cuisines may be found, ranging from plant-based diets that are abundant in vitamins, minerals, and fibre to animal-based meals that are heavy in protein. Indigenous grains, herbs, and medicinal plants are all components of traditional tribal food consumed by tribal peoples believed to promote complete health. This review highlights the rich diversity and cultural heritage of indigenous tribal foods across India, emphasizing their potential to promote sustainable nutrition and the preservation of traditional knowledge.

title: Vishnukundina Empire
abstract: Abstract The Vishnukundins were a dynasty ruling in the eastern Deccan in the 5th and 6th centuries ce , who played an important role in the geopolitics of the Deccan through their military campaigns and matrimonial alliances. The extent of their control has been conjectured on the basis of the provenance of their coins through the present‐day Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra regions. Their patronage of Buddhist and brahmanical institutions is known through their endowments and construction activity, although no monument can clearly be dated to this period.

title: SANSKRIT HERITAGE OF TIRUVALLA
abstract: Cultural heritage of a people refer the social and religious attitudes, beliefs, principles and conventions of behavior inherited from the traditions stretching back to remote antiquity. It also includes in its connotations intellectual and artistic manifestations in the form of language, literature, art, music and more importantly customs, rituals and food habits developed by the society from generation to generation. Kerala finds mention in the annuals of international trade from as early as 3000BCE, having established itself as the major spice trade centre of the world and traded with Sumer. The earliest written record specifically mentioning Kerala is contained in the Sanskrit work known as the Aitareya Aranyaka . Later, such figures as Katyayana and Patanjali exhibited in their writings a casual familiarity with Kerala’s geography. Megasthanes, the Greek Ambassador to the court of Emperor Chandragupta Maurya mentions in his work Indica on many South Indian States, including Automela (probably Muziris), and a Pandian trade centre. A 3rd century BCE rock inscription by Emperor Asoka the Great, references Kerala as Keralaputra. All these point toward the very ancient Sanskrit heritage of Kerala prior to the Christian era where Tiruvalla also opens its on accounts simultaneously.

title: Exploring the Food Culture and Dietary Practices of the Thakar Tribe in Ahilyanagar District, Maharashtra
abstract: Food culture refers to the practices, attitudes, and beliefs as well as the networks and institutions surrounding the production, distribution, and consumption of food. This ethnographic study delves into the food culture of the Thakar tribe of Udadwane Village, an agrarian community who used to be hunters and gatherers, utilizing participant observation, interviews, and rapport establishment. The aim is to study the culinary practices, dietary pattern, beliefs, taboos, seasonal changes and rituals associated with the food and underscores the importance of recognizing food as more than mere sustenance. The findings shows that rice is the staple food of the tribe. The daily meal includes bhaat, waran and bhakar. They are dependent on forest produce and kitchen-garden. They consume a wide variety of wild vegetables throughout the year like Kaudar, kaili, haredi. The consumption of crabs holds a significance in various life events and rituals of Thakars. Food restrictions, particularly observed by pregnant women, highlights cultural beliefs and taboos. The Thakar tribes’ connection to the nature is evident in every meal-from foraging in the forests to cultivating their own crops. The communal aspect of food preparation and consumption strengthens social bonds and ensures that their cultural heritage remains vibrant and alive, rooted in the very flavours that define them.

title: The Role of Theatre Artists in the Development, Preservation, and Promotion of Telugu Theatre in Kadapa District: A Study
abstract: Theatre is one of the oldest performing arts that reflects the cultural, social, and historical identity of a society. Kadapa District (YSR District), Andhra Pradesh, has played a significant role in the development of Telugu theatre through the dedication of numerous theatre artists, drama organizations, and traditional performing groups. The district is widely recognized as the birthplace of the Surabhi Theatre movement, which has preserved mythological, historical, and social dramas for more than a century. Theatre artists from Kadapa have contributed immensely as actors, directors, playwrights, musicians, stage designers, costume designers, and cultural educators. Their efforts have promoted Telugu language, literature, and cultural heritage while inspiring future generations. However, modernization, digital entertainment, and financial challenges have adversely affected traditional theatre. This study examines the contributions of theatre artists toward the development, preservation, and promotion of Telugu theatre in Kadapa District. Using historical and descriptive research methods, the study analyzes their artistic achievements, cultural significance, institutional support, and contemporary challenges. The findings emphasize the need for documentation, digital preservation, financial assistance, and policy support to ensure the sustainability of Telugu theatre

title: A Study: Inclusion of generational slang in UX writing in India
abstract: Traditional architecture of Rajasthan incorporates a variety of elements that make it both aesthetically pleasing and climate-responsive, ensuring functional and passive design. These architectural features have potential to adapt to the harsh climate and cultural preferences of the region. The use of sandstone, Jaali, and wood creates a sense of warmth and beauty, while the use of windcatchers, courtyards, thick walls, and overhangs helps to keep the buildings cool in the hot desert climate. Therefore, this paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the the aesthetics and functional benefits of integrating traditional architecture elements of Rajasthan in new developments. The integration of traditional architectural elements into contemporary building designs has gained significance as a means to harmonize cultural heritage with modern development. This review paper investigates the aesthetics and functional benefits of incorporating traditional architecture elements from Rajasthan, India, into new developments. The paper discusses the implications of this integration for climate responsive design, cultural preservation, and the creation of distinctive and contextually relevant architectural expressions. This comprehensive analysis contributes to the discourse on architectural innovation, bridging the past with the present and guiding the future of design by embracing the rich legacy of Rajasthan's architectural heritage.

title: SHILPASMRITI: DIGITAL PRESERVATION OF ANCIENT TEMPLES
abstract: Ancient temple inscriptions constitute invaluable historical records that document linguistic evolution, dynastic history, socio-cultural practices, and religious traditions. However, continuous exposure to environmental degradation, biological growth, and human interference has rendered many inscriptions fragile and increasingly illegible. Manual documentation methods are time-intensive and require specialized epigraphic expertise, limiting large-scale preservation efforts. This paper presents ShilpaSmriti, an AI-driven digital preservation framework designed to automatically capture, interpret, translate, and archive ancient South Indian temple inscriptions. The proposed system integrates image preprocessing, script identification, optical character recognition (OCR), neural machine translation, and cloud-based storage to convert inscription images into searchable, multilingual digital records. Scripts such as Tamil-Brahmi, Grantha, Old Kannada, and early Telugu are processed using script-specific OCR pipelines. Experimental evaluation demonstrates effective text extraction, reliable translation, and secure long-term preservation through cloud infrastructure. The framework enables global accessibility to inscription data while safeguarding cultural heritage from physical deterioration

title: <b>Effect of Fashion on Indian Society: A Socio-Economic and Cultural Study</b>
abstract: Fashion is a dynamic social phenomenon, reflecting changing lifestyles, economic conditions, cultural ideals and technological innovations. The Indian fashion business has evolved from traditional apparel linked to local identities to a worldwide enterprise typified by consumerism, digital media, globalization and celebrity culture. On one hand the Indian fashion business has changed the social behaviour, identity formation and shopping habits and on the other hand it has expanded into becoming one of the primary contributors to economic growth, employment creation and preservation of culture. This paper discusses the effect of fashion on Indian society from the sociological, technological, economic and environmental perspectives of the society. The present study is an attempt to explore the function of fashion in the development of social identity, promotion of cultural heritage, generation of employment, women empowerment and economic progress. The research is based on secondary data from government papers, academic publications, company records and market research. It also addresses themes like quick fashion, environmental damage and changing cultural expectations. Our research results show that fashion is an important engine for economic development and modernization, but sustainable and culturally sensitive policies are needed for balanced social development.

title: Shanxi-Shaanxi Merchants, Bangzi Opera and the Cult of Guan Gong on the Lu Canal in the Ming and Qing Dynasties
abstract: Regarding the Grand Canal from Beijing to Hangzhou, it was not only a transportation route for transporting grain from the south to the north, commercial travel, and water conservancy irrigation, but it was also a cultural belt that integrates the diverse regional cultures of Qi-Lu, Yan-Zhao, Chu-Han, Huai-Yang, and Wu-Yue. Over the span of five and a half centuries, merchants from Shanxi and Shaanxi exerted a profound influence along the canal during the Ming and Qing dynasties (1368-1912). Taking the Lu Canal, also known as Huitong River in Shandong as a research thread, this paper explored the cultural and commercial activities of Shanxi and Shaanxi merchants who established guild halls, set up theatres, and worshipped the God of Guan along the canal during the Ming and Qing dynasties. These activities not only facilitated the spread of the clapper theatre, but also promoted the widespread inheritance of the worship of Guan Gong, further consolidating the cultural influence of the Shanxi and Shaanxi merchant clans. By studying these phenomena, this paper revealed how Shan-Shaanxi merchants connected commerce and culture through guild culture, enriching the social and cultural heritage along the Lu Canal.

title: From Ephemeral to Eternal: Role of Archival Practices in Safeguarding the Performing Arts
abstract: Performing Arts – encompassing dance, music, theatre and other similar disciplines reflect a vital dimension of intangible cultural heritage, highlighting their identity, historic essence and artistic expression. However, their transient nature renders them susceptible to loss, distortion and misinterpretation. Archival practices are not just a mere passive repository of historical records; it serves as a dynamic force that both safeguards and rejuvenates the long artistic tradition, and also a highly crucial source for preservation of these art forms, as it involves systematic documentation with appropriate codification for the advantage of posterity. This paper investigates the role and importance of archival practices in safeguarding the multifaceted aspects of Performing Arts and examines how archives maintain authenticity, promote metadata standards, and facilitate the continuation of intangible traditions; while simultaneously, it acts as a dynamic source and a vibrant tool for academic inquiry such as scholarly research work, teaching, and innovative reinterpretation. Through a qualitative synthesis of institutional case studies, community archives, and various initiatives on heritage preservation, this study underscores the diverse role of archival practice and confirms that it not only preserves history but act as a catalyst for tradition, continuation, and innovation in the realm of performing arts.

title: THEATRICAL DEVOTION: UNVEILING THE SPIRITUAL DYNAMICS OF ANKIYA BHAONA WITHIN BHAKTI
abstract: Ankiya Bhaona, through its founder, the 15th-century Vaishnavite saint Sankaradeva (1449-1568), presents a unique theatrical tradition of Assam, India. This paper explores the spiritual dynamics of Ankiya Bhaona to highlight its place in the Bhakti movement. The study examines the historical development, cultural influences, and devotional elements that define Ankiya Bhaona. Originating from Sankaradeva’s classic “Cihna Yatra,” (Pageant on Painted Scenes) Ankiya Bhaona blends Sanskrit drama with Assamese folk traditions, creating a powerful medium for spiritual expression. These narratives, primarily regarding the lives and deeds of Krishna and Rama, are performed in Namghars (prayer halls), reinforcing community engagement and devotion. The paper portrays the unique features of Ankiya Bhaona through a comparative analysis with other Bhakti performances, emphasizing its use of indigenous cultural elements and its roles as religious and social gatherings. This study also considers the symbolism and metaphors employed in the performances, showing their part in deepening the audience’s spiritual experience. This paper underlines that Ankiya Bhaona is essential not only in the community’s life but also as a guarantor of cultural continuity, making it an integral part of Assamese cultural heritage.

title: Analysing Facial Dynamics - Navarasas in Kathakali Videos Using Deep Learning
abstract: Indian classical and folk dances are visual treats for the audience; the expressions used by the artist are crucial in conveying the narrative of the accompanying music to the audience. Kathakali – a classical dance rooted in the southern Indian state of Kerala, combines storytelling with eye-catching attire, face masks, and makeup. Facial expressions and hand gestures play an essential role in this process, as they are the primary means of communication between the dancer and their audience. Kathakali is widely prevalent among Kerala attractions for tourists, entertainment, and temple rituals. Fathoming the facial expressions of Kathakali artists is crucial for fully conceiving and appreciating the art form. Facial expressions in Indian Classical dance forms called Navarasa use a range of facial expressions through which a dancer can connect with their audience and draw them into the story they are trying to tell. The process of identifying and understanding Kathakali expressions has been automated to facilitate recognition and analysis. In addition to aiding in the preservation of cultural heritage, the focus has been placed on identifying and classifying the facial expressions used in Kathakali performances. A combination of ViT and LSTM networks was applied to observe Kathakali Bhava, or facial expressions, from videos, achieving an accuracy of 96.67%.

title: Power, Memory, and Resistance: The Politics of Contesting the Hitchcock Memorial in Kerala
abstract: Power, Memory, and Resistance: The Politics of Contesting the Hitchcock Memorial in KeralaDr. Sivadasan PThe politics of colonial commemoration in India left behind a contested landscape of statues and memorials, many of which became focal points of nationalist resistance after independence. This study examines the trajectory of the Hitchcock Memorial in Kerala, erected in 1928 at Valluvambram in Malabar to honour R. H. Hitchcock, the District Police Superintendent who led the suppression of the Malabar Rebellion of 1921. Intended by the colonial state as a symbol of imperial valour and deterrence, the memorial was immediately challenged by nationalist leaders. It became the subject of satyagraha campaigns, public protests, and political resolutions. Its relocation to the Malabar Special Police Camp in 1969 and eventual demolition of the restored structure at the police camp in 1988 reveal the shifting meanings of colonial monuments in postcolonial Kerala. By tracing the memorial’s contested afterlife, this paper situates the Hitchcock Memorial within broader debates on colonial commemoration, nationalist resistance, and postcolonial memory politics. The analysis highlights how imperial symbols were reinterpreted, resisted, and replaced by memorials to indigenous struggles, such as the ‘Wagon Tragedy’ Memorial. The Hitchcock Memorial thus serves as a lens for understanding the dynamic interplay among power, memory, and resistance, demonstrating that monuments are not static relics but rather evolving sites of historical contestation in the public sphere.

title: Birhors and their Cultural Practices
abstract: This publication explores the cultural heritage and traditional lifestyle of the Birhor tribe, a traditionally nomadic forest-dwelling community (Adibasis) primarily located in the Purulia district of West Bengal, as well as parts of Jharkhand, Odisha, and Chhattisgarh. The study provides a detailed anthropological and sociological overview of the community, which is categorized into two main groups: the nomadic Uthlu (or Bhulia) and the settled Janghi (or Thania). Key areas of focus include: Social Structure and Lineage: An analysis of the patrilineal society, including various clans (such as Hembram, Murmu, and Marandi) and their associated totems. Cultural Rituals: Documentation of life-cycle rituals related to birth, death, and marriage, including the five distinct forms of Birhor marriage (Bapla) and the significance of the "Naya" (chieftain/priest) and "Mati" (exorcist). Economic Practices: Traditional occupations such as hunting, gathering, and the specialized craft of making rope from the "Cihore" creeper. Religious Beliefs: An overview of the Birhor pantheon, centered on Sing Bonga (the Sun God), and the various festivals observed, such as Soharay, Karma, and Sarhul. Socio-Economic Challenges: A review of the community's current status, including government efforts toward permanent settlement at Bhupati Palli and the ongoing challenges regarding health, education, and nutrition.

title: The Development of Indonesian Marriage Law in Contemporary Era
abstract: Indonesia is a highly diverse country, comprising a multitude of tribes, groups, races, and religions, and is endowed with a rich cultural heritage. The heterogeneity of Indonesian society provides the context for interfaith and other forms of marriage. The specific legislation that governs marriage is Law Number 1 of 1974. It is commonly assumed that Law No. 1/1974 requires immediate revision due to its outdated nature and inability to address contemporary issues pertaining to marriage. Consequently, there are numerous provisions within the Marriage Law that require amendment or addition. For instance, there is a need to introduce more robust penalties for those who violate the Marriage Law, whether they are involved in interfaith marriages, same-sex marriages, polygamous marriages, or marriages contracted without the requisite formalities. This study aims to examine the evolution of marriage law in Indonesia and the challenges it has faced. It employs a descriptive qualitative approach with a literature review. The findings reveal that Indonesia's marriage regulation has undergone three distinct phases, each characterised by its own set of issues. Additionally, the country's marriage law has experienced two distinct periods: one following independence and the other following the enactment of Marriage Law Number 1 of 1974.

title: Cultural Revival and Artistic Consciousness: Tagore and Okakura Tenshin
abstract: The paper is about the contributions made by two influential cultural leaders Rabindranath Tagore and Okakura Tenshin to revitalize the awareness of cultural and artistic consciousness in their particular societies. Tagore was an Indian polymath and Okakura was a Japanese philosopher and art historian, and was greatly involved in the act of transforming his culture in the era of social and political upheaval. Tagore's writing, singing, and painting made a contribution to an ethos of universal humanism that aimed to revive the link between the Indian society and its own traditional cultural heritage and also got inspiration from the cultural trends all over the world. Similarly, Okakura philosophy of art and culture was all about preserving the traditional Japanese aesthetics against the tide of westernizations. Both of these people, even though they came from different cultural backgrounds, stressed the need for the revival of the culture in an increasingly globalized world. By comparing the different methods they use to preserve culture and their art, this paper illuminates the similarities between their thought process and artistic philosophy. It also looks at how their works continue to inspire and influence cultural movements today making a case for the relevance of their ideas in the global discourse on art and culture today.

title: Visible Weapons, Invisible Woes
abstract: The traditional khukuri is an important cultural marker of the Indian-Nepali community which is often seen as a symbol of Gorkha valor. In the Nepali community, the khukuri is an essential part of wedding ceremonies, religious, and death rituals and many even believe it to be a container of sacred energy. While this weapon is much celebrated as a marker of valor and Nepali pride, the makers of this weapon are often not a part of mainstream discourse, and quite undeservedly so, being Nepali Dalits. Revisiting social customs and items related to the cultural study and the politics of social inclusion and exclusion, this paper attempts to spell out this unique situation of caste within the background of the larger national identity of Nepali pride, valor, and loyalty, symbolized by the khukuri. The paper aims to interrogate and unveil the mainstream Indian-Nepali discourse, especially in the Darjeeling Hills which has continued to turn a blind eye to the Nepali Dalits and overlook their contribution to the cultural heritage of Nepali people to the larger narrative. Hence, it is a study of the culture, history, and society of the Darjeeling Hills to provide a more comprehensive and inductive view of the Nepali Dalits, the makers of khukuri whose lived reality within the larger community is often overlooked and goes unseen.

title: Existence and Importance of Kumbh-Parva in the Vedas
abstract: The Kumbh Parva, an ancient religious festival, holds significant cultural and spiritual importance in Indian society. This sacred gathering is based on the Vedic principles and is one of the largest religious congregations globally. The festival’s origins can be traced to ancient Vedic texts, where the word "Kumbh," meaning "pitcher," has multiple interpretations symbolizing purification, abundance, and spiritual unity. The festival, held at specific sacred locations like Prayag, Haridwar, Ujjain, and Nashik, symbolizes a confluence of physical, mental, and spiritual cleansing. In the Vedas, Kumbh is associated with the divine and is described as a means to purify the body and soul, allowing participants to attain spiritual liberation. The festival also promotes social unity, devotion, and human cooperation, transcending individual differences. The Vedic scriptures, such as the Rigveda, Samaveda, and Atharvaveda, all reference the Kumbh, linking it with both material and spiritual blessings. The Kumbh festival is thus not only a celebration of faith but also a manifestation of India’s rich cultural heritage, where each action, be it bathing in the holy rivers or meditating, is considered to purify the individual. Through its spiritual essence, Kumbh serves as a reminder of the importance of virtuous deeds and the eternal pursuit of happiness and liberation.

title: Innovative Handicraft Embroidery Dress Marketing with ArtiicialIntelligence(AI):AnalysingEffectiveness and CustomerEngagement with Sustainable Model
abstract: The field of handicraft embroidery dresses is of crucial importance in terms of cultural heritage, skilled artisans, sustainable earnings, and fashionable looks. Regardless of all mentioned factors, there are still problems with limited market coverage, lack of understanding of customer needs, poor branding, and strong competition from manufactured fashion products. In recent years, Artificial Intelligence (AI) the basis for innovations in the area of marketing by providing opportunities for personalization, predicting customer behavior, automating processes, and engaging buyers. This research paper aims the use of AI in marketing innovations of handicraft embroidery dresses with a particular emphasis on effectiveness and customer engagement. Based on a thorough literature review, this research identifies several AI-based instruments used in the marketing process: recommendation systems, chatbots, visual searches, social media analytics, and demand forecasting. According to the results of the paper, AI-powered marketing positively influences customer engagement, conversion, brand communication, and sustainability while causing the issue of digital illiteracy and loss of authenticity. The proposed fuzzy model further contributes by addressing uncertainty in consumer behaviour and providing a structured framework to evaluate the interplay between technological intelligence, cultural value, and engagement outcomes.

title: Preserving Temple Heritage through Immersive Technologies: A Case Study of Odisha
abstract: Abstract Odisha’s temple heritage represents one of the richest architectural and cultural traditions in India, yet many of its monuments remain vulnerable to environmental degradation, urban pressure, structural decay, and limited public accessibility. This paper explores the potential of immersive technologies, particularly Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR), and 3D digital documentationas innovative tools for preservingtemple heritage in Odisha. Using a case study approach, the paper examines how the aged old temples such as Konark, Lingaraj, and Mukteswarand others can be digitally documented and re-presented to create interactive heritage experiences. It argues that immersive technologies not only support conservation by generating accurate visual records, but also enhance education, tourism, and cultural engagement by enabling users to experience monuments beyond physical and geographical constraints. At the same time, the study critically reflects on the challenges such as technological cost, authenticity, digital ethics, and infrastructural limitations in heritage institutions. By situating Odisha’s temple heritage within the broader discourse of digital preservation, the paper highlights how immersive technologies can bridge gap between traditional conservation and contemporary digital innovation, offering new lens for the preservation of sacred and architectural legacy of the region for future generations. title: Soft Power and Cultural Diplomacy: The Influence of India in Malaysia
abstract: India's use of soft power and cultural diplomacy has significantly influenced Malaysia, reflecting a strategic approach to strengthening bilateral relations and promoting cultural affinity. This abstract explores the mechanisms and impacts of India's soft power in Malaysia, focusing on cultural, educational and economic dimensions.India leverages its rich cultural heritage, including films, music, dance, cuisine, yoga, and festivals to build a positive image and foster a sense of cultural kinship with Malaysia. The Indian diaspora in Malaysia is one among the largest population outside India, plays a crucial role in sustaining and propagating Indian culture. Cultural festivals such as Diwali, Pongal andThaipoosam celebrated widely in Malaysia, serve as platforms for cultural exchange and mutual appreciation. This research paper focuses on few research enquires like how India's soft power and cultural diplomacy have successfully created a favorable and conducive environment for bilateral cooperation, promoting cultural understanding, and strengthening socio-economic ties between India and Malaysia. Further it explores the hidden soft power effect by which the strategic use of cultural assets and educational initiatives continues to shape a positive narrative and enhance India's influence in the region.

title: Economic Impact, Cultural Diplomacy, and the emergence of Spirituality-Driven Global Tourism
abstract: Spiritual tourism represents one of the fastest-growing segments of the global travel industry, blending wellness, cultural heritage, and religious exploration into transformative visitor experiences. This paper examines the socio-economic dimensions of spiritual retreats and ashram tourism, with a focused case study on the World Cultural Festival (WCF) organized by the Art of Living Foundation. Drawing on empirical data from two landmark editions — New Delhi, March 2016, and Washington D.C., September 2023 — the paper quantifies the substantial economic spillover effects of large-scale spiritual events, including foreign exchange earnings, hotel revenue surges, tax generation, wage creation, and international tourist inflows. The paper further explores how ashram-based tourism clusters around institutions such as the Art of Living International Centre (Bengaluru) generate sustained economic activity, foster cross-cultural dialogue, and contribute to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Findings suggest that spiritual tourism, when institutionally anchored and professionally managed, can rival conventional cultural tourism in measurable economic output while simultaneously delivering intangible social value.

title: Jødeforfølgelse Med Socialistisk Fortegn. Janina Katz’ Forfatterskab Mellem Polen Og Danmark Med Særligt Henblik På Romanen Putska
abstract: Abstract Introducing life and work of Janina Katz, the article undertakes an analysis and interpretation of her second novel, the autofictional Putska . Born on the second of March 1939, Katz belonged to a renowned Jewish family with numerous members, of whom, however, only her mother and she survived the Second World War. Their extraordinary family history may be traced in practically all of Katz’ writings, as can her Jewish cultural heritage. The novel Putska is no exception. Its composition, characters and the image it gives of life in Cracow are examined in order to make understandable the protagonist’s decision to exile herself from Poland and migrate to Denmark, much like the author herself. 1969, having fled from that revival of anti-Semite harassment which was launched by the political leadership of socialist Poland, Katz was granted asylum in Denmark, where she soon learned the language to a perfection which enabled her to unfold a widely acknowledged literary work which does not cease to speak of her unique life experience. Central perspectives on her life and work include migration, autobiography, Jewishness and social and cultural history of Poland.

title: From Ephemeral to Eternal: Role of Archival Practices in Safeguarding the Performing Arts
abstract: Performing Arts – encompassing dance, music, theatre and other similar disciplines reflect a vital dimension of intangible cultural heritage, highlighting their identity, historic essence and artistic expression. However, their transient nature renders them susceptible to loss, distortion and misinterpretation. Archival practices are not just a mere passive repository of historical records; it serves as a dynamic force that both safeguards and rejuvenates the long artistic tradition, and also a highly crucial source for preservation of these art forms, as it involves systematic documentation with appropriate codification for the advantage of posterity. This paper investigates the role and importance of archival practices in safeguarding the multifaceted aspects of Performing Arts and examines how archives maintain authenticity, promote metadata standards, and facilitate the continuation of intangible traditions; while simultaneously, it acts as a dynamic source and a vibrant tool for academic inquiry such as scholarly research work, teaching, and innovative reinterpretation. Through a qualitative synthesis of institutional case studies, community archives, and various initiatives on heritage preservation, this study underscores the diverse role of archival practice and confirms that it not only preserves history but act as a catalyst for tradition, continuation, and innovation in the realm of performing arts.

title: Cultural Continuity and Change: A Study of the Sixteen Samskaras in Modern Hindu Society
abstract: This paper explores the cultural continuity and changes surrounding the sixteen samskaras within modern Hindu society. Drawing from a synthesis of scholarly works and classical texts, the study examines the historical significance and contemporary relevance of these rituals. Ramaswami Aiyer, Pandey, and Shelat provide foundational insights into the cultural heritage of India, emphasizing the enduring nature of the samskaras and their role in shaping Hindu identity. Shrutiprakashdas, Dave, Shukla, Vivekpriyadas, and Gnaneshwardas offer philosophical, sociological, and cultural perspectives, elucidating the spiritual dimensions and adaptive qualities of these ceremonies in response to societal shifts. Through an analysis of these sources, this paper seeks to understand how the sixteen samskaras continue to uphold tradition while accommodating changes in modern Hindu society. The Sixteen Samskaras, deeply rooted in Hindu philosophy and tradition, represent a series of sacred rites of passage that mark significant milestones in an individual’s life journey. These rituals, spanning from conception to cremation, play a vital role in shaping the spiritual and cultural identity of Hindus across different regions and communities. Each samskara is imbued with profound meaning and symbolism, reflecting the rich tapestry of beliefs and practices that define Hinduism.

title: EARTHSCRAPERS: A SUSTAINABLE URBAN HOUSING ALTERNATIVE IN THE ERA OF LAND SCARCITY
abstract: Rapid urbanization and population growth are intensifying the global challenge of land scarcity, particularly in megacities where horizontal expansion threatens ecosystems and cultural heritage. While skyscrapers have maximized space, they also contribute to urban heat islands, energy inefficiency, and visual congestion. As a response, the concept of earthscrapers inverted skyscrapers built below ground emerges as a sustainable alternative. By utilizing subterranean space, earthscrapers conserve surface land, provide natural thermal insulation, and reduce environmental footprints while maintaining access to light and ventilation through advanced engineering. This paper critically examines the architectural, environmental, and socio-economic dimensions of earthscraper housing, exploring its integration with renewable energy, urban resilience, and biodiversity preservation. Drawing on case studies and feasibility analyses, the study highlights both opportunities and barriers including engineering challenges, social acceptance, and regulatory gaps. Findings suggest that, although still experimental, earthscrapers represent a transformative approach to sustainable urban living in land-constrained cities. They underscore the need for forward-looking urban design strategies that balance human habitation, ecological integrity, and cultural preservation.

title: Nrithya: A Curated Image Dataset of Indian Folk and South Indian Classical Dance Forms
abstract: This study presents two carefully curated image datasets capturing the rich visual diversity of Indian folk and classical dance forms. The first dataset focuses on four South Indian classical dance styles - Bharatanatyam, Kathakali, Kuchipudi and Mohiniyattam - initially comprising 410 images, expanded to 1,621 through image augmentation. The second dataset encompasses six Indian folk dances - Bhavai, Garba, Karakattam, Malwai Giddha, Toda and Yakshagana - growing from 600 to 2,368 images after augmentation. All images were sourced from publicly available online platforms and YouTube videos, ensuring diversity in performers, regional styles, costumes and poses. Preprocessing techniques such as background removal and Canny edge detection were applied for costume-based feature extraction, and their effectiveness was systematically evaluated. This work addresses a critical gap in the availability of ethnically representative dance datasets by providing curated collections to support a range of computer vision tasks, including posture recognition, dance form classification, and cultural analytics -thereby contributing to both cultural heritage preservation and AI-driven dance research.

title: Better than Disneyland!
abstract:
The Museum of Skanderborg in Denmark invited everybody who had an interest, to take part in an excavation during the annual autumn school break. The object to be excavated was a poorhouse dating to the end of the 19th century. Usually something like that would not become the object of an excavation, due to its young age. However, the Museum of Skanderborg strives to do things differently. We aim to be significant, and to be an institution of value and pride to the local community. Being a small museum requires new means to make an impact.
The notion of a public excavation started to evolve, and the poorhouse seemed the perfect object. Apart from researching the history of the poorhouse in the local archives, planning was mostly on a practical level. Nothing on this scale had been done before in Denmark, so it was sort of like flying a kite. It was impossible to predict anything concerning finds, as well as participants!
It turned out to be a huge success. One family drove across the country to join the dig, and visitors as well as the press were constantly present. When an 8 year old kid claims that this is better than Disneyland, you know you did something right.
My aim is to discuss whether a more informal setting might be furtive. A setting in which the Museums also demand something of the participants, so that they get a notion of being important in this particular project. A joint venture to reach back and reveal history. Are we ready to share this mission? Can we gain anything from a shared mission? Is touching a couple of hundred people aiming too low, or it is worthwhile getting fewer people really engaged?

title: From Capture to Engagement: A Reproducible Workflow for 360° Virtual Tours and Audience Evaluation of Sacred Kerala Temple Murals
abstract: Abstract Documenting reproducible workflows is a recognized gap in Digital Humanities scholarship, particularly for sacred heritage digitization where tacit methodological decisions around ethics, capture, authoring, and evaluation are rarely made explicit. This paper addresses that gap through a fully documented, pipeline for creating and assessing 360° virtual tours of Kerala temple murals, demonstrated through the Chemmanthatta Mahadeva Temple, Thrissur, central Kerala. What distinguishes this workflow from comparable digital heritage projects is the intersection of three methodological commitments rarely combined in a single pipeline: (1) ethically governed capture of a living, ritually active sacred site; (2) darśan-sensitive authoring that preserves the spatial and devotional logic of the temple interior; and (3) an embedded audience evaluation instrument designed to measure culturally specific perceptions of aura, sacredness, and authenticity in a virtual environment. Together, these commitments surface the “hidden costs” of sacred heritage digitization that standard workflows leave unaddressed. The workflow comprises five documented stages. In the first stage, Ethical Capture, permission had to be obtained from both local temple administration and Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), Thrissur Circle. ASI regulations mandated certain requirements regarding the placement of cameras, use of flash photography, and entry into the sanctum sanctorum itself, all of which were respected and included in the workflow process; specifically, the ritual lines of sight involving the deepasthambham and balipeetham were retained in the panoramic views. Community approval protocols were used to allow for publishing of devotional images and minimize participant responses. In the second stage, Contextual Authoring, panoramas of 360° views were edited in Affinity Photo 2 and imported into Articulate Storyline 360, chosen because of its hotspot navigation tools and minimal coding required for humanities scholars. The final product will offer annotations about mural iconography but maintain the temple experience from entry to sanctum. If a team does not have access to Articulate Storyline 360, the pipeline was designed with enough detail to recreate using open-source software options such as Pannellum or A-Frame. Thirdly, evaluation design incorporates the implementation of a purpose-designed survey embedded directly into the tour. The measurement tool includes ten items measuring on a Likert scale three constructs: aura/presence, sacredness/reverence, and authenticity/fidelity, along with two additional items for comparing physical and virtual darśan. Aura is defined and operationalized based on the ritualized embeddedness approach suggested by Benjamin, elaborated by Kenderdine and Yip in terms of digital facsimile; sacredness is based on the definition of darśan as a relational experience with a divine image by Eck; and authenticity is understood and measured from both material (accuracy of reproduction) and experiential (genuineness of experience) perspectives. The definitions have been developed specifically to consider cross-cultural differences in perceptions, as some respondents are likely to perceive the above-mentioned constructs from the perspective of people unfamiliar with Kerala temple culture. The fourth stage was the deployment and data collection process where the tour had been hosted on the web. Data have been collected using n=100 individuals who came from a diverse community made up of professionals in heritage, art history students, and general public. The backgrounds of the participants were captured as covariates to test the effect that previous knowledge of darśan has on perceived virtual sacredness. This could minimize novelty bias by acclimating the participant to the 360° interface before evaluation questions were asked. Analysis and Archiving: The fifth phase involved exporting descriptive statistics in CSV format and coding the qualitative answers manually. Analysis so far reveals that respondents with experience with temple worship felt higher levels of sacredness and presence but authenticity was relatively consistent, implying that visual realism is more universal compared to the experience of worshiping. All assets used in this project are version-controlled at GitHub under the CC BY-SA 4.0 license, including panoramas, 360 Storyline template with its branching, survey form as an independent Google Form, raw data schema. Portability is an essential consideration in the workflow design. The five-step process can be generalized from this particular temple; any team engaging with a heritage site that requires institutional clearance, spatial reasoning, and culturally sensitive appraisal can leverage this model. Chemmanthatta temple is only a concrete example of the more generalizable process rather than a special case. Through articulation of the ASI negotiating protocols, darśan-oriented UX design principles, and consent-based approaches inherent in similar projects but usually unspoken of, we aim at developing an ethically sustainable virtual heritage system consistent with DARIAH's approach.

title: Sacred Ecology and Community Beliefs: Indigenous Environmental Ethics and the Conservation of Springs in Kashmir
abstract: Human societies have historically depended upon the natural environment for survival, resulting in the emergence of complex cultural practices that regulated the use and protection of natural resources. Although the expansion of civilization and technological advancement significantly improved human living conditions, they also accelerated the exploitation of ecosystems and the degradation of natural heritage. In many traditional societies, however, indigenous belief systems and religious practices functioned as informal mechanisms of environmental governance by attributing sacred value to elements of the natural landscape. Such cultural perceptions often discouraged unsustainable exploitation and promoted long-term ecological stewardship. Focusing on selected springs and caves of the Kashmir Valley, this paper explores how religious beliefs, local traditions, and customary practices have contributed to the preservation of these natural heritage sites. It argues that sacred landscapes have historically served not merely as places of worship but also as effective instruments for community-based environmental conservation, offering important lessons for contemporary heritage management and sustainable resource conservation.

title: Assessment of Land Use/Land Cover Change, Rainfall Pattern and NDVI in Nandyal District, Andhra Pradesh: Using Geo-Informatics
abstract: Nandyal District is blessed with pilgrimage heritage sites and spans over 9,681 square kilometres, with diverse ecosystems and varieties of trees occupying about 32% of the land. Looking at the land usage pattern from 2017 to 2024, it is evident that the main activity is farming. Crops occupy about 52.74% of the land in 2024, with rangelands and forests slightly decreasing. It is evident that the rainfall pattern is diverse during these years. It is clear that the growth of crops depends on the rainfall pattern. NDVI shows the diversity in the growth of vegetation. It is evident that the areas with high rainfall are occupied by moderate to dense greenery. It is also evident that the relationship between rainfall and NDVI is not straightforward. More rainfall does not imply the growth of vegetation in all areas, especially those with low rainfall. In summary, it is evident that the change in land usage, the distribution of rainfall, and the growth of vegetation show the importance of sustainable land usage. It is important to maintain the requirements of farming while protecting the land. Continuous research is required to come up with strategies to address the challenges brought about by global warming and urbanization.

title: Preserving Temple Heritage through Immersive Technologies: A Case Study of Odisha
abstract: Abstract Odisha’s temple heritage represents one of the richest architectural and cultural traditions in India, yet many of its monuments remain vulnerable to environmental degradation, urban pressure, structural decay, and limited public accessibility. This paper explores the potential of immersive technologies, particularly Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR), and 3D digital documentationas innovative tools for preservingtemple heritage in Odisha. Using a case study approach, the paper examines how the aged old temples such as Konark, Lingaraj, and Mukteswarand others can be digitally documented and re-presented to create interactive heritage experiences. It argues that immersive technologies not only support conservation by generating accurate visual records, but also enhance education, tourism, and cultural engagement by enabling users to experience monuments beyond physical and geographical constraints. At the same time, the study critically reflects on the challenges such as technological cost, authenticity, digital ethics, and infrastructural limitations in heritage institutions. By situating Odisha’s temple heritage within the broader discourse of digital preservation, the paper highlights how immersive technologies can bridge gap between traditional conservation and contemporary digital innovation, offering new lens for the preservation of sacred and architectural legacy of the region for future generations. title: Hybrid Clustering and Classification Framework for Ground Penetrating Radar Data Analysis
abstract: Summary Ground-penetrating radar (GPR) is a powerful, non-invasive, and non-destructive geophysical tool widely used for subsurface investigations in a variety of applications such as environmental monitoring, infrastructure condition assessment, archaeology, civil engineering, and resource exploration. Despite its advantages, manual interpretation of GPR data remains a time-consuming and subjective task, often influenced by operator experience and prone to error. In this study, we present a comprehensive, open-source, Python-based framework that leverages modern signal processing and machine learning techniques for the automated and efficient analysis of GPR data. Our workflow utilizes GPRPy, an open-source software package designed specifically for GPR data processing and visualization, combined with robust machine learning libraries including scikit-learn and PyTorch. The processing pipeline begins with advanced signal preprocessing methods to enhance data quality and interpretability. Key preprocessing steps include dewow filtering to remove low-frequency noise, time-zero correction to align signals temporally, and Laplacian of Gaussian (LoG) edge detection to highlight subtle subsurface features. Subsequently, multiple features such as amplitude, variance, signal energy, and peak prominence are systematically extracted and normalized to ensure consistency across datasets. For subsurface pattern identification, we apply a suite of clustering algorithms — Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM), Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN), and KMeans — enabling unsupervised recognition of geological and man-made anomalies. Following clustering, a hybrid classification approach combining Random Forest classifiers and Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU)-based deep neural networks is employed to accurately categorize detected features, achieving classification accuracies exceeding 90% on labeled datasets. This integrative framework significantly accelerates GPR data interpretation, reduces operator bias, and enhances the reliability of subsurface characterization. Furthermore, the open-source nature of this pipeline facilitates reproducibility, transparency, and future enhancements, including potential integration with multi-frequency GPR systems and complementary geophysical sensors for improved subsurface imaging

title: Kashmir Valley As A Timeless Tourist Destination: A Historical Study
abstract: Kashmir Valley has long been celebrated as a timeless tourist destination, attracting travelers, pilgrims, scholars, and rulers across centuries. This qualitative study explores the historical evolution of tourism in the Kashmir Valley by examining travel accounts, historical texts, cultural traditions, and heritage sites. From ancient times, Kashmir served as a center of spiritual pilgrimage, learning, and natural retreat, drawing visitors due to its scenic landscapes, sacred shrines, and rich cultural life. During the medieval period, Sufi traditions, Mughal patronage, and artistic developments further enhanced the valley’s appeal. In the colonial and post-colonial eras, Kashmir emerged as a prominent leisure destination, shaping modern tourism infrastructure while retaining its historical charm. The study highlights how geography, culture, spirituality, and hospitality collectively contributed to Kashmir’s enduring tourist identity. By emphasizing continuity and transformation, the paper underscores the historical depth of tourism in Kashmir Valley and its significance in understanding the region’s cultural and economic heritage.
